title: Image standard opens form a basis after graded scalar extension
statement: Let R,S,A,B be commutative rings with the stated algebra structures, let 𝒜 and ℬ be graded submodules, let β : S ⊗_R A ≃ₐ[S] B and ψ : 𝒜 →+*ᵍ ℬ satisfy β(1 ⊗ a)=ψ(a), and suppose every ℬ_n is the S-span of ψ(𝒜_n), with the irrelevant ideal of ℬ mapping into that of 𝒜. Then the opens basicOpen ℬ (ψ f), indexed by positive homogeneous f in 𝒜, form a topological basis of Proj ℬ.

source.place: Tag 01N2, standard-open covering argument from homogeneous spanning

proof.text: STATEMENT-DISPUTED: Let k be a field, R=k, S=k[t], A=k[x] and B=k[t][x], with degree given by the exponent of x and coefficients of degree zero. Take beta to be the canonical scalar-extension isomorphism and psi the coefficient inclusion. Then B_n=S*x^n is the S-span of psi(A_n), and the image of the irrelevant ideal (x) is (x). Every positive homogeneous f in A is c*x^n for c in k. If c=0 its image standard open is empty; otherwise it equals all of Proj B, since c is a unit and every Proj point avoids x. But Proj B is Spec k[t], with the nonempty proper open D(t). Thus these opens cover Proj B but do not form a basis. The old proof incorrectly inferred containment D(psi(f_i)) <= D(b) from a nonzero summand at one prime. Withdraw this false split. Its sole parent now uses the affine image cover from Mathlib Proj.mapAffineOpenCover and quasi-coherence, keeping its statement unchanged.

proof_origin.place: Tag 01N2 gives an image standard-open cover, not an image standard-open basis; counterexample and withdrawal of the false split.
